dictionary.install_linux_step_1: Open Terminal on the Linux computer.
dictionary.install_linux_step_2: Paste the command and press Enter.
dictionary.install_linux_step_3: Return here and approve the connection request.
dictionary.install_windows_step_1: Press the button below: a single ready-made file, Nuxiva_Setup.exe, is downloaded.
dictionary.install_windows_step_2: Open Nuxiva_Setup.exe from your Downloads folder: it installs and pairs the PC by itself.
dictionary.install_macos_step_1: Open Safari on your Mac and go to the address below.
dictionary.install_macos_step_2: Sign in with your Nuxiva account.
dictionary.install_macos_step_3: From the File menu choose Add to Dock: Nuxiva will open in its own window, like an app.
dictionary.install_esp32_step_1: Build and upload the firmware from client_satellite/microcontrollers/esp32 with pio run -t upload.
dictionary.install_esp32_step_2: Connect the board by USB to the Nuxiva server and detect the USB ports.
dictionary.install_esp32_step_3: Start guided setup: enter the Wi-Fi details, the board generates its own key and is paired after your confirmation.
dictionary.install_linux_guide: Open Terminal on the Linux computer. Paste the command below, press Enter and approve the connection request on this page. You need Python 3, curl and an account with sudo access.
dictionary.install_windows_guide: No setup, no ZIP and no extra files: you only need the Windows PC to connect.
dictionary.install_macos_guide: The macOS package is in preparation. Guided enrollment still requires a verified installer compatible with Mac.
dictionary.install_esp32_guide: The firmware is verified in CI with host tests and a build, but has not yet been proven on a real board. Uploading the firmware remains manual.
dictionary.install_esp32_no_ports: No USB ports detected. Connect the board with a data cable and try again.
dictionary.windows_download_hint: The file already contains the one-time code that pairs the PC: keep it private and use it before it expires.

dictionary.pc_link_hint: You do not need to install the full Nuxiva server on the second PC; Linux and Python 3 are enough. Copy and run this command on that PC to install the small Nuxiva agent, then approve its request on this page. If the server uses a local HTTPS certificate, install the Nuxiva CA on the PC first.
dictionary.pc_code_hint: Alternatively generate a code and use --code CODE instead of --join. Codes expire after ten minutes.
dictionary.res_hint_calm: The machine has headroom: everything stays active and only screens covered by others stop drawing.
dictionary.res_hint_elevated: Idle things are unloaded sooner and caches over budget are cleaned.
dictionary.res_hint_high: Saving mode: unused models and screens are unloaded to stay responsive.
dictionary.res_hint_critical: Maximum saving: voice, security and rescue stay guaranteed, everything else is freed.

dictionary.install_android_guide: Install the Nuxiva app on a phone, tablet or TV, then link it to this server with a QR code or a 6-digit code. Every code works once and expires in minutes.
dictionary.install_android_step_1: Press the download button or scan the first QR code with the device, then install the APK (allow installs from this source when Android asks).
dictionary.install_android_step_2: Press Generate code here: a QR code and a 6-digit code appear, valid for a few minutes and usable once.
dictionary.install_android_step_3: Open the Nuxiva app and choose Scan the code. If you cannot scan, type the server address and the 6-digit code instead.
dictionary.android_apk_qr_alt: QR code with the link to the Android app
dictionary.android_apk_hint: The file comes from the official releases and is signed. Compare the SHA-256 if you want to verify it.
dictionary.android_enroll_qr_alt: QR code to link the device
dictionary.android_enroll_hint: Keep it private: whoever knows it before it expires can add a device. It works once and the device checks the fingerprint.
dictionary.android_error_android_apk_unavailable: The Nuxiva app is not published yet or the releases cannot be read.
dictionary.android_error_enroll_https_unavailable: Open the console through the secure address of the server (HTTPS) to generate a code.
dictionary.android_error_enroll_ca_missing: The server has no certificate authority yet. Enable the secure connection first.
dictionary.android_error_enroll_too_many_tokens: Too many codes are waiting. Revoke one or wait for it to expire.
dictionary.android_error_generic: The code could not be generated. Try again shortly.
dictionary.install_android_step_4: Check that the fingerprint shown on the device matches the one here, then confirm.
dictionary.android_state_code_used: The code was entered on the device: confirm there to finish.
dictionary.android_state_enrolled: Device linked. It now appears in the nodes list.
dictionary.android_state_expired: The code has expired. Generate a new one.
dictionary.android_state_revoked: Code revoked: it can no longer be used.

dictionary.windows_pairing_code_desc: Generate a single-use code valid for 10 minutes to enter into the 'Connect this PC to NUXIVA' window:
dictionary.windows_step_1_full: Download and run Nuxiva_Setup.exe on your Windows computer.
dictionary.windows_step_2_full: On launch, the 'Connect this PC to NUXIVA' window opens: enter the server address shown above and click 'Verify'.
dictionary.windows_step_3_full: Generate the 6-digit code below, enter it into the assistant, and click 'Connect'. The node will appear online within seconds.
dictionary.windows_not_appearing_alert_title: Already installed the Windows version but it does not appear in the nodes list?
dictionary.windows_not_appearing_reason: If you downloaded the installer from GitHub Releases or selected 'Use in local mode (without server)' on launch, the assistant is running on your PC in isolated offline mode. To link it and show it in the list, follow these quick steps:
dictionary.windows_troubleshoot_step_1: 1. Locate the glowing Nuxiva orb on your screen or the tray icon in the taskbar (bottom right).
dictionary.windows_troubleshoot_step_2: 2. Right-click the orb or tray icon and choose 'Settings' (or press Ctrl + Alt + Space).
dictionary.windows_troubleshoot_step_3: 3. At the bottom of the Settings window, click the red 'Unlink this PC' button: the pairing window will reopen immediately.
dictionary.windows_troubleshoot_step_4: 4. Paste the server address shown above, generate and enter the 6-digit code, and click 'Connect'.
dictionary.windows_troubleshoot_reset_tip: Alternative Windows reset: Close Nuxiva from the taskbar, press Win + R, type %APPDATA%\NUXIVA and delete assistant.json. Restarting the assistant will immediately reopen the pairing window.
dictionary.windows_firewall_note: Note: If Windows Defender Firewall shows a prompt, select 'Allow access' on private networks. If the server is on another PC, make sure the address is not 'localhost' but the local IP (e.g. 192.168.x.x).
